main_text.p: Soli animam extrahit. Præcipitatur etiam perse ac figitur Tincturis Martis, Veneris ac Solis: maximè v. nutritur lacte suo, de quo illud Sybillæ Emmeriæ fortasse interpreteris, cum inquit: Sedens superse-dē stratam, dans illi jus proprium, id est lac de cœlo missum quod identidem tamen potest ad Lapidem universalem applicari, in fragmentis Sybillinis Philippi de Lignamine Equitis Siculi. De hoc etiam Gebri dictum accipias, qui inquit: Si ex solo Mercurio (ex minerali nempe licet aliunde parato) Lapidem conficere nôris, præstantissimæ indagator eris naturæ. Hinc Basilius in curru triumphali pag. 88. Etenim Mercurius (inquit) est purus putus ignis penitus. Quapropter à nullo igne cumburi potest, nullus eum captivat ignis ad destructio-

page.notes: Marginal mark at left "N5" is a faint reference mark, not clearly legible. Several words in the italic/underlined passage are set in mixed type and some letters are uncertain (e.g. "strat-am", "Gebri"); the running head and page number are clear. The final word "ætio-" is a catchword-like hyphenated fragment continuing onto the next page; it is kept in the text as a line.
